request.description:
## Before you send anything

**1. Point `{{baseUrl}}` somewhere you are allowed to write to.**
Every request in folders 3, 5 and 6 writes to whichever database the host resolves to. The default is the live site.
Use the local harness (same PHP, same `.htaccess`, same schema) until you trust the shape of a body:

    baseUrl = http://127.0.0.1:8099/api
    siteUrl = http://127.0.0.1:8099        ← media lives here, not under /api

**2. Run `1 · Auth → Login`.**
It fills `{{token}}` and `{{csrf}}` for every other request and sets an `admin_token` cookie. Both are 64-char
hex and last 7 days (`expires_in: 604800`). There is no refresh and no revoke endpoint — if a token is
compromised, delete its row from `auth_tokens`.

**3. Fill in `{{adminEmail}}` and `{{adminPassword}}`** in the collection's Variables tab. They are deliberately
empty and are never committed. Do not put them in a URL — they would land in shell history and Postman sync.

## The three rules that explain most failures

| Symptom | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `401 unauthorized` | Missing/expired `X-Auth-Token`. |
| `403 forbidden` | Missing or wrong `X-CSRF-Token`. Only POST/PUT/DELETE check it. |
| `415 content-type must be application/json` | The header is absent or does not *start* with `application/json`. |

## What "editing content" actually costs

- **Editing an existing row** is live on the next page load. The PHP API is authoritative at render time — no rebuild.
- **A brand-new `slug`** needs `npm run build` + a deploy first, because its route shell, OG tags and sitemap entry are prerendered.
- **Media** is a two-step dance: upload to get a URL, then PUT the URL into the field. Media fields store strings, never files.

## Field-by-field contract

Folder `4 · Field reference` has one request per entity whose description is the full field table —
type, required, max length, JSON shape and the exact validation each type performs. That table is generated
from `api/entity-schema.php`, the same file `crud.php` validates against, so it cannot be out of date.

**A `max` in that table is the editorial ceiling, not always the ceiling that rejects you.** Most text
columns in the database are narrower than the 255 the schema promises (`skills.grp` is `VARCHAR(40)`,
`projects.year` is `VARCHAR(20)`). `crud.php` now validates against the smaller of the two, so an
over-long save answers `422` naming the field and its real limit instead of a bare `update failed`.
The measured widths are in `site/API.md` §4.1 and repeat in every field table.

Regenerate it after touching the schema:

    cd site && npm run postman

request.description:
Profile writes are a `REPLACE INTO`, so **POST creates and updates with the same call** — there is no separate create path.

`k` must match `[a-z0-9_]{1,60}` or you get 422 `invalid key`. `v` must be a string; `null` gives 422 `v must be text`. Sending a number, array or object is rejected even though JSON would coerce it.

Response: 201 on POST, 200 on PUT, both `{"ok": true}`.

This writes to whichever database `{{baseUrl}}` points at — set it to your local harness before running anything here.

⚠ **`profile` has no `published` column, so a created row is on the live site immediately.** Run Delete as soon as you are done checking.

request.description:
PUT is the only place `previous_k` matters. Send the new `k` **and** the old one; the API deletes `previous_k` and replaces `k`. Omit `previous_k` and it defaults to `k`, so the row is overwritten in place rather than renamed.

**This is how you avoid orphans:** renaming without `previous_k` leaves the old key live, and the site keeps reading it.

item.name: 6 · Media

header.description: Required.
Required. Can be sent as a `csrf_token` form field instead — one is included below.

request.description:
Multipart form. Field **`file`** carries the image; field **`folder`** (default `uploads`) picks the sub-directory.

**Do not copy the JSON `Content-Type` header onto this request** — Postman sets `multipart/form-data` and its boundary for you, and a hand-written header without a boundary makes PHP see zero files, which answers 400 `no file uploaded` rather than anything about content-type.

## Limits, and the status each one returns

| Condition | Code | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Missing/unreadable `file` | 400 | `no file uploaded` |
| `folder` outside `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,59}` | 400 | `invalid folder` |
| 0 bytes or over **8 MB** | **413** | `file must be between 1 byte and 8 MB` |
| mime outside jpeg/png/webp/avif/gif | **415** | `only JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or GIF images are allowed` |
| Bytes pass the mime test but are not a decodable image | 415 | `file is not a readable image` |
| Directory or `move_uploaded_file` fails on the host | 500 | `could not store the upload` |

The mime check uses `finfo` on the bytes, not the filename — renaming a `.php` to `.webp` does not get it in. An SVG is rejected outright, which is deliberate: an SVG can carry script and would execute on your own origin.

## What you get back

`201 {path, url, mime, bytes, width, height}` where `url === path`, shaped `/media/uploads/<folder>/<folder>-<8 hex>.<ext>`. Anything over 2400 px on a long edge is resampled with GD first, so the returned `width`/`height` may be smaller than what you sent. The random 8-hex name means the same file uploaded twice produces two distinct paths — there is no dedupe and no overwrite.

A `media` library row is inserted best-effort: if `api/v2-schema.sql` has not been imported the insert fails silently and the upload still succeeds. Never treat the media library as the source of truth; the file on disk is.

**The limitation that matters for app screenshots:** this writes only inside `/media/uploads/`. The site's app icons and screenshots live at `/media/apps/<slug>/`, which this endpoint cannot reach — placing a file there is a filesystem operation, not an API call.

formdata.description: Sub-directory inside /media/uploads/. Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens; must not start with a hyphen; ≤ 60 chars.
Belt-and-braces: the header above already satisfies the check.

request.description:
Static file — served straight from disk, no PHP, no token, no CSRF. If this 404s, the upload wrote a path the web server cannot see (a docroot mismatch); if it 200s, the URL is safe to PUT into an `image` field.

Note the base: media lives at the **site root**, not under `/api`, which is why this uses `{{siteUrl}}` where every other request uses `{{baseUrl}}`.

Recipe: full round-trip on one app

request.description:
Run these in order and watch the site between steps — this is the whole content model in five calls:

1. `1 · Auth → Login`
2. `5 · Admin CRUD → Apps → Create — every field` (captures `{{appId}}`, `published: 0` so nothing is visible)
3. `6 · Media → Upload image`, then `Recipe: upload → attach to an app`
4. `5 · Admin CRUD → Apps → Publish / unpublish` — reload `/apps`, the card appears with no rebuild
5. `5 · Admin CRUD → Apps → Delete` — the card disappears

If step 4 shows nothing, the public list is cached or the row's `sort_order` pushed it off the first screen; this request answers 200 with only `published = 1` rows, so compare its count against the admin list.
